title: First transatlantic telegraph cable
summary: In August 1858 the telegraph ships Niagara and Agamemnon, having spliced the cable mid-Atlantic on 29 July, landed its two ends at Trinity Bay, Newfoundland, and Valentia Island, Ireland, by 5 August. Queen Victoria and President Buchanan exchanged the first official messages from 16 August, but the cable failed within a few weeks.

uncertainty.note: IEEE Spectrum has the Niagara arriving in Newfoundland on 4 August; Scientific American has her anchoring at 1:45 A.M. on 5 August. Sources give no exact failure date (valentiaisland.ie: within three weeks).

as_recorded.value: On 29 July, as Field recorded in his journal, the two ships spliced
On 5 August 1858, both ships reached their destinations
At 5 15 A. M. the telegraph cable was landed

where.modern_name: Valentia Island, County Kerry, Ireland and Trinity Bay, Newfoundland (cable ends)
where.historical_name: Valentia, Ireland and Trinity Bay, Newfoundland (cable ends; Newfoundland telegraph house at the head of Bull Arm per Scientific American)

waypoints.date: 4-5 August 1858 (IEEE gives 4 August arrival, Scientific American 5 August landing)
waypoints.label: Trinity Bay, Newfoundland: western end; the telegraph house was at the head of Bull Arm. Point is the bay.
Valentia Island, Ireland: eastern end, landed 5 August. Point is the island centre.

importance.justification: The first working telegraph link between continents, even though it failed within weeks.

beats.caption: The Niagara and Agamemnon splice the cable mid-Atlantic, then each steams toward its own shore, paying the cable out behind.
The cable is landed at Trinity Bay in Newfoundland and at Valentia in Ireland, joining the two continents.
Queen Victoria and President Buchanan exchange the first official messages, but the cable stops working within a few weeks.
